title: CFA classes in Abu Dhabi: 1-on-1 coaching or a classroom course?
excerpt: Group classes, self-study and 1-on-1 coaching each suit a different CFA candidate. How to tell which one you are, and what each costs per hour, before you pay for anything.

seo.title: CFA Classes in Abu Dhabi: 1-on-1 Coaching vs Classroom
seo.description: How 1-on-1 CFA coaching compares with group classes and self-study in Abu Dhabi: pace, schedule, feedback, cost per hour and who each suits.

sources.title: CFA Program: Level I and Level II exams

points: There are three ways to prepare for CFA Level I or II: a group class, self-study, or 1-on-1 coaching. Most candidates who pass combine two of them.
A group class gives you a timetable and classmates. 1-on-1 coaching gives you feedback on your own mistakes. Self-study gives you neither, but costs least.
Do a timed set of practice questions before you choose. Your score by topic tells you how much teaching you need.

blocks.text:
You have registered for CFA Level I or Level II, or you are about to, and you live or work in Abu Dhabi. You expect to spend 300 hours or more on the curriculum[^cfa], most of them around a full-time job or a degree. The question is where your paid hours should go.

We teach CFA 1-on-1, so read this knowing that. We have tried to say plainly when a group class or self-study is the better choice.

**Group class.** An instructor teaches the curriculum to a class in a fixed order, in a room or on a video call. You get a timetable, classmates and a teacher to ask. The pace is set for the class, not for you.

**Self-study.** You read the CFA Institute curriculum or a prep provider's notes and work the practice questions alone. It is the cheapest route and the most flexible, and the easiest one to fall behind on.

**1-on-1 coaching.** One instructor, one candidate. Sessions start from the questions you got wrong, so time goes to your weak topics and skips the ones you already know. It costs more per hour than a class seat, but you usually need fewer hours.

blocks.text:
1. **Take a timed test first.** Do 30 to 40 questions under exam timing, for example from the [CFA Question Bank](/cfa/questions). Write down your score by topic.
2. **Count your hours honestly.** Weeks to the exam multiplied by hours you can really study each week. If that is well under 300, you need help using the hours well, not more material.
3. **Find what is actually holding you back.** If you understand the reading but run out of time, you need practice. If you can't follow the reading at all, you need teaching. If you keep putting off study, you need a timetable.
4. **Match each gap to a format.** Practice is self-study. Teaching is a class or a tutor. A timetable is a class or booked sessions.
5. **Price the hours.** Multiply the hours of help you need by the hourly rate, and compare that with a course fee that covers every topic, including the ones you don't need taught.
Worked example: a working analyst in Abu Dhabi

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
- Choosing by brand name before taking a single practice test.
- Paying for teaching on topics you can already score well on alone.
- Leaving mock exams to the last week, when there is no time left to fix what they show.
- Believing any format guarantees a pass. None does. Your own practice hours decide it.

This framework assumes you can judge your own practice results honestly. Many candidates can't at first, which is what a diagnostic is for. It also says nothing about the quality of a particular class or tutor: a good group teacher beats a weak 1-on-1 one. Ask for a trial session or a diagnostic before paying for any of them, including ours.

items.q: Where can I take 1-on-1 CFA classes in Abu Dhabi?
items.a: We teach CFA Level I and Level II 1-on-1, in person at your home in Abu Dhabi or live online anywhere in the UAE. Every course starts with a free 30-minute diagnostic.

items.q: How much does 1-on-1 CFA coaching cost?
items.a: AED 150 an hour, or AED 3,000 a month for 30 hours, which is AED 100 an hour. CFA Institute exam and registration fees are separate and paid to CFA Institute.

items.q: Do I still need the CFA Institute curriculum?
items.a: Yes. The exam is set on it, and coaching works from its practice questions.

items.q: Is 1-on-1 better than a group class?
items.a: Not for everyone. A group class suits candidates who want a fixed routine and classmates. 1-on-1 suits candidates whose time is short and who know, or want to find out, exactly where they lose marks.
